To overcome this, we present Sigma , the first large-scale (3B/8B) continuous dLM built on steerable, low-dimensional ODE/SDE latent trajectories. Trained blockwise via likelihood optimization, Sigma jointly denoises Gaussian-corrupted token embeddings while learning an optimal embedding geometry. To accelerate training, Sigma leverages pre-trained weights from autoregressive (AR) models for warm-starting. During inference, we identify classifier-free guidance and score temperature as essential for high-fidelity reasoning and coding. Across comprehensive math reasoning and coding evaluations against state-of-the-art discrete counterparts (masked dLMs and AR baselines), Sigma achieves competitive performance with discrete models on standard benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, Minerva, HumanEval, MBPP) after pre-training and on challenging reasoning tasks (e.g., MATH-500, AIME) after supervised fine-tuning. Beyond performance parity, we uncover key structural properties unique to continuous dLMs: ( i ) embedding-space steering effectively governs the quality-diversity trade-off, yielding strong pass@ k k performance and ( ii ) continuous trajectories enable graceful degradation for low NFEs and efficient distillation. These establish continuous dLMs as a promising paradigm for efficient language generation. 1 Introduction While diffusion language models (dLMs) enable fast parallel decoding compared to autoregressive (AR) baselines ( Inception Labs et al., 2025 ; Song et al., 2025 ; Fu et al., 2026 ) , dominant discrete dLMs operate in high-dimensional, categorical state spaces (e.g., V ≥ 100 ​ K V{\geq}100\text{K} ) that suffer under limited step budgets and impede trajectory control for complex reasoning and coding tasks. Continuous diffusion offers a principled way to overcome these structural limitations through smooth latent geometries that natively support structured editing ( Meng et al., 2022 ) , flexible ODE trajectory steering ( Lu et al., 2022 ) , and efficient few-step distillation ( Salimans and Ho, 2022 ; Song et al., 2023 ) . Recently, there has been growing interest in continuous diffusion and flow matching for text generation ( Gulrajani and Hashimoto, 2023 ; Dieleman et al., 2022 ; Hu et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ; Guo et al., 2026 ; Liang et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) ; see App. A . However, existing methods remain limited in scale ( < 2 ​ B <2\text{B} ) or focus on unconditional generation, lacking evaluations on complex reasoning tasks. Whether continuous dLMs scale to complex conditional reasoning remains open. This is a non-trivial hurdle because continuous models update block embeddings globally, in contrast to the factorized categorical denoising of discrete dLMs that leads to semi-autoregressive token commitment per block. To overcome these limitations, we present Sigma (3B/8B): s cal i ng up G aussian diffusion m odels for l a nguage. We propose a family of continuous dLMs operating over a 16-dimensional embedding space trained blockwise via likelihood optimization. Within each block, the model learns to jointly denoise Gaussian-corrupted token embeddings and to structure an optimal embedding geometry. To scale training, we warm-start the model from existing pre-trained AR weights. For inference, we explore diffusion trajectory sampling, identifying embedding-space Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) and Score Temperature (ST) as crucial ingredients for high-fidelity reasoning and coding. Through unified evaluations against state-of-the-art discrete dLMs (e.g., Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion ( Fu et al., 2026 ) , LLaDA ( Nie et al., 2025b ) , Dream ( Ye et al., 2025 ) , SDAR ( Cheng et al., 2026 ) ), we show that Sigma achieves competitive performance across standard math and coding benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, Minerva, HumanEval, MBPP) and extends well to harder reasoning tasks after supervised fine-tuning (e.g., MATH-500, AIME). Beyond raw accuracy, we highlight two structural properties unique to continuous language diffusion: ( i ) flexible pass@ k k exploration–exploitation control via CFG and ST hyperparameters; and ( ii ) graceful performance degradation under low NFE regimes (16/32) and efficient trajectory distillation for very low NFE regimes (4/8). Together, these properties position continuous diffusion as a promising foundation for fast inference in modern agentic AI. Our key contributions are summarized as follows: • First Large-Scale Continuous dLM: We present Sigma (3B/8B), efficiently trained by warm-starting from pre-trained AR weights, and optimizing a regularized continuous diffusion ELBO. • Competitive Math & Coding: Across six base and ten instruct benchmarks, Sigma achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art discrete dLMs/ARs on reasoning and coding. • Inference Steering (CFG & ST): By elucidating the inference design space, we show that embedding-space CFG and ST effectively govern the quality-diversity trade-off with minimal latency overhead via single-pass block-causal attention packing. • Low-NFE Robustness: With embedding regularization, Sigma sustains strong quality down to 16 NFEs per block, while trajectory distillation noticeably improves performance at 4–8 NFEs. 2 Background Notation.
